(a) internal hypothermia, (b) hemodilution, and (c) low flow rates are three concepts that obviate the use of blood for priming.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a blood substitute for priming of the extracorporeal circuit is feasible, and that this is the best way to avoid hemodilution.
the bloodless perfusion system can be used for up to 4 hours without blood transfusions, which is the time limit for the use of cardiopulmonary bypass in cardiac surgery.
the heart-lung apparatus can be primed with a blood substitute without the use of any blood, and without the need to add any blood to the circuit during the course of perfusion.
